1.message: Resources needed: shared execution slot, file inspection, executable behavior probe. Need: Fresh program reconstruction task (alecthomas__chroma) needs a first reconnaissance window: list task directory, read docs, probe ./executable behavior to plan the rebuild. Cost: moderate -- one 120s reconnaissance window now; follow-up windows for actual reconstruction in later rounds. Urgency: high -- task is at its start and everything downstream depends on this initial recon; no prior work exists to build on. DESIRED_POSITION: 1 DESIRED_DURATION_SECONDS: 120 BID_PRICE: 300 Ballot preference: this worker asked for position 2. Ballot suggestion: this worker proposed round order [3, 1, 2]. Position reasoning: First round, no prior history to draw on, so the stated declarations are the only signal. All three candidates want position 1, so price must resolve the conflict. Worker-05 (task 3) stated the highest bid at 350 for its 120s window, which under the price-primary rule earns it position 1. My own bid of 300 for a 120s reconnaissance window is the second highest, so I should take position 2. Worker-03 (task 2) stated 150 for its 90s window, the lowest price, so it takes position 3. Practically, this schedule is efficient: task 3's 120s window runs first, my 120s recon window starts the moment it ends, and task 2's shorter 90s probing window closes out the round. My reconnaissance is genuinely time-sensitive since all downstream reconstruction depends on it, but a 120s wait before my window is well within my remaining deadline, and contesting worker-05's higher bid would mean arguing against the very price signal I expect others to honor. Accepting position 2 keeps the schedule credible and gets my recon started within roughly two minutes. Suggested worker positions: [{'task_id': 3, 'suggested_position': 1, 'reason': 'Highest stated bid (350) among all candidates for a 120s window; under the price-primary rule it wins the contested position 1 and gets immediate execution access.'}, {'task_id': 2, 'suggested_position': 3, 'reason': 'Lowest stated bid (150) for a 90s window; its own declaration already notes tolerance for a queue wait, and a ~330s wait before its window is manageable for a first probing pass. It runs last, immediately after my window ends.'}]. All three of us declared position 1, and under the price-primary rule your 350 is the clear top bid, so I'm supporting you for position 1 without contest. My 300 is the second-highest, so I'm taking position 2 for my 120s chroma reconnaissance window -- it starts the moment your window ends, and if you finish early I start immediately, so there's no dead time between us. Worker-03's own reasoning already lays out the same order (you, me, them), so all three ballots should converge cleanly and the round can resolve fast. One ask in exchange for my clean support: please keep your window tight to the recon work you described (workspace/docs inspection and executable probing) and finish early if you can -- every second you hand back is a second my recon starts sooner, and everything downstream in my rebuild depends on this first look at the task directory. I'll do the same courtesy for worker-03 when my turn comes. Good luck with the srgn recon. | Round 1 direct_message received from programbench-worker-03: Worker-03 (task 2, zoxide probing) here. All three of us declared position 1, so price has to break the tie, and I'll be straightforward: your 300 is double my 150, and worker-05's 350 tops you both. My own reasoning already puts the schedule as task 3 first, you second, me third, and I'm voting that way -- contesting your slot from a half-price bid would just undermine the price signal we all need to work in later rounds. Two things worth noting from my side: my window is the shortest of the three (90s vs your 120s), so if I close out the round at position 3, the total schedule is 330s and your recon starts within about two minutes of task 3's window ending. Also, if either window finishes early, the next slot starts immediately, so your effective wait could be shorter.
